districts.name: The Royal Quarter
districts.character: The crown of the city, on the plateau (ground 72-78, the highest broad land) with a cliff down to the ravine pond on its west and a drop to the harbour on its south. The palace (landmark, about 44x36, three to four storeys with corner towers and a central oxidised-copper dome) stands on the highest flat ground (x -2568..-2524, z 285..345, floor ~75), its gate facing north down the King's Way, with a stepped forecourt rising from the plateau road (~65) up to it. The cathedral (landmark, about 36x22 plus a tall copper spire, the city's tallest thing, seen from everywhere) stands on the east rise (x -2515..-2482, z 272..315, floor ~74), its west front on a small cathedral close. Fill in with the finest buildings in the city: a chancery, the bishop's house, a guard barracks and a few great noble houses, all in smooth stone and calcite with tall mullioned windows and colonnades. The dip at x -2512..-2480, z 318..349 (ground 62-64) is the royal garden: terraces, a long fountain basin and a stair down toward Harbour Street.

districts.name: The Grand Market
districts.character: Where the north avenue, the west avenue (over the river bridge) and the King's Way meet, on gentle ground 66-72 (middle ~69). The grand market (landmark, a paved square about 30x30, floor ~69) fills the middle, with spruce and dark-oak stalls, a central fountain and a market cross; its north side opens onto the west avenue. Around it, facing the square: a guildhall with an arcaded ground floor and a copper-capped clock tower (the district's second landmark building), a corn exchange, two inns and tall merchants' houses three storeys high with shop fronts, all fine pale stone with blue banners. The west edge is the river quay (market-west street runs along the water): one or two plots can be riverside warehouses. Busy, grand, arcaded.

districts.name: The Harbour
districts.character: The city's lake front, low and working, behind the lake wall. West part (x -2610..-2565) is flat shore at 61-65: the harbour basin (landmark, a walled stone quay with piers and a lake gate, partly over water at the box's south edge), warehouses with hoist beams, a customs house and a fish market. A rocky spur (x -2560..-2536, ground 68-80) runs south into the lake as a peninsula: put a lighthouse or harbour tower on it and a chapel for sailors. The east part (x -2530..-2479) is low shore at 60-63 with boathouses half over the water, a ropewalk and sailors' lodgings. Plainer than the city above: stone-brick plinths, diorite and calcite walls, dark roofs, lots of spruce (doors, cranes, jetties). Harbour Street runs along the north edge and the harbour avenue down the east edge to the shore.

districts.name: Kingsgate West
districts.character: The finest town houses outside the palace, on the west side of the King's Way between the market and the plateau, ground 62-71 rising east (from the river side ~63 to the avenue ~69). One row of tall stone town houses (three to four storeys, about 11x10 walls on 15x22 plots) facing the King's Way and the south ring, with copper gutters, carved stone door cases and small walled back gardens toward the river; the western end looks over the river where it leaves the city. Rich, ordered, symmetrical facades.

districts.name: Kingsgate East
districts.character: Fine town houses east of the King's Way, ground 62-73. Two old sinkholes break the ground (one at about x -2540..-2533, z 238..256, one at x -2528..-2512, z 228..242): don't build over them, make them the district's garden square, a fenced sunken garden with a fountain and benches that the houses face. Three- and four-storey stone houses, as fine as Kingsgate West, fronting the King's Way, the plateau road and the garden, with colonnaded ground floors on the King's Way side.

districts.name: Merchants' Row
districts.character: The wealthy merchants' street east of the market, ground 63-72. Pairs of tall three-storey merchant houses with a counting room or shop on the ground floor and warehouse lofts above, fronting the market-east street, the west avenue and Copper Lane; a bank or money-changers' hall on the corner by the market. Fine but less grand than Kingsgate: calcite and diorite with smooth-stone trim, shutters in dark oak. A small pond near the east edge (around x -2482, z 150..170, just north of the box, and its edge inside) can become a little garden.

districts.name: The River Quays
districts.character: The east bank of the river through the north of the city, between the water and the north avenue, ground 63-72. A quay street along the water with boathouses and a watermill partly over the river, barge warehouses, a brewery and a tannery downstream, and plain terraced houses on the avenue side. The bank narrows southward (at z 150 the river is at x -2608..-2592, leaving only ~25 blocks): the southern plots are shallow and long. Plain stone with spruce timber, less trim; one detail: a covered footbridge or water stairs down to the river.

districts.name: Northgate
districts.character: The plainest residential district, just inside the north wall and east of the north avenue, ground 63-72 and gentle. Rows and terraces of two-storey town houses on lanes running east-west off the north avenue (the planner lays them), a small well square with a parish church in the middle, a bakery, a smithy near the north gate and a gatehouse inn on the avenue. A pit drops to ~51 around x -2496..-2480, z 90..102: leave it as a fenced pond or yard. Stone-brick ground floors, plain calcite upper floors, deepslate roofs, few ornaments.

districts.name: The Craftsmen's Quarter
districts.character: Workshops of every trade on the west bank, ground 63-78: a low hill (x -2742..-2712, z 64..112, ~76) in the west and the mill pond (x -2692..-2677, z 96..115) in the middle. Forges and a foundry with big chimneys, masons' and carpenters' yards, weavers' and dyers' houses near the mill pond and the river (dye vats, drying racks), a glassworks, coopers, the guild hall of the smiths. Buildings are two storeys, wide and sturdy: workshop on the ground floor, home above, yards behind. Plainer stone, more spruce and dark oak, smoke and clutter; the river bank (east edge) gets a fulling mill and a timber wharf.

districts.name: The Scholars' Quarter
districts.character: Learned and quiet, on the west bank south of the west avenue, ground 63-82: the observatory hill rises in the west (top ~82 at x -2744..-2728, z 170..185). The library (landmark, about 30x20, three storeys with a copper dome and a long reading hall of tall mullioned windows, floor ~68) stands on the gentle middle ground facing the west avenue; an observatory tower with a copper dome crowns the hill; a college around a cloistered courtyard, a school, a printing house, an apothecary and masters' houses fill the rest. Fine pale stone, a little plainer than Kingsgate; small walled gardens and a garden square with a fountain between the library and the college. The south edge looks over the river where it leaves the city.
